summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count on from any starting number between 1 and 20.
Count backward from any number between 10 and 1.
Read and write numerals 0 to 20 and use them to show how many objects.
Say number names in order while counting, matching one number to each object.
Show that the last number counted tells how many, whatever the order or arrangement.
Show that each next number in the count means one more object.
Recognize groups of up to 5 objects in familiar patterns without counting.
Use a number to tell how many objects are in a set.
Compare two or more groups of objects as more, fewer or the same.
Compare two written numbers from 1 to 10 to tell which is more or less.
Build and break apart 11 to 19 as a ten and some extra ones.
Show addition and subtraction within 10 with objects, drawings or other representations.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Break numbers up to 10 into two parts in more than one way.
Find the number that makes 10 with any number from 1 to 9.
Describe several measurable features of an object, such as length or weight.
Compare two objects by a shared measurable feature, such as which is taller.
Understand basic ideas of time and the tools used to measure it, such as clocks and calendars.
Know the names of the seven days of the week.
Recognize the four common coins: penny, nickel, dime and quarter.
Name shapes in the world, knowing a shape's name does not change with size or turn.
Describe where objects are using position words like above, below, beside and behind.
Describe features of shapes and use them to sort a group of shapes.
Draw or build simple flat shapes.
Put simple shapes together with manipulatives to make larger shapes.
Sort objects into given groups and count how many are in each.
Compare the counts of sorted groups using words like more and fewer.
Count to 120 starting from any number below 120.
Read and write numerals to 120 and use them to show how many objects.
Count backward from any number between 20 and 1.
Count by fives up to 100, starting from 5, 10, 15 or any other multiple.
Understand ten ones as a bundle called a ten.
Understand two-digit numbers as made of tens and ones.
Compare two two-digit numbers with >, = or <.
Count by tens up to 120 starting from any number.
Add numbers with totals up to 100.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a number mentally, without counting.
Add or subtract a multiple of 10 to or from a two-digit number and explain why.
Solve addition and subtraction problems within 20.
Solve problems that add three whole numbers with a total up to 20.
Learn what the equal sign means and judge addition or subtraction equations true or false.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation with three numbers.
Use properties of operations as strategies for adding and subtracting.
Solve subtraction by finding the missing addend.
Find sums and differences with numbers up to 20.
Add and subtract within 10 fluently.
Tell defining from non-defining shape features; build and draw shapes with given features.
Put together and take apart flat and solid shapes to see how parts make wholes.
Recognize flat and solid shapes seen from different views and turned different ways.
Cut circles and rectangles into halves or fourths and name the parts and whole aloud.
Put three or more objects in order by length.
Compare two lengths indirectly by measuring both against a third object.
Measure a length or distance by laying copies of a smaller object end to end.
Read and write clock times to the hour and half hour, on dial and digital clocks.
Know the values of a penny, nickel, dime and quarter.
Collect, organize and show data with up to three categories.
Make conclusions from simple data displays such as object graphs, pictographs, T-charts and tallies.
Understand three-digit numbers as hundreds, tens and ones.
Understand ten tens as a bundle called a hundred.
Count within 1,000 by 1s, 10s and 100s from any number.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in words, digits and expanded form.
Compare two three-digit numbers with >, = or <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently.
Find the sum of as many as four 2-digit numbers.
Add and subtract within 1,000 and justify the answer.
Use how addition and subtraction undo each other to solve problems.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 within 1,000.
Write and solve addition and subtraction problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently.
Tell if a set up to 20 is odd or even; count by 2s; write evens as doubles.
Total the objects in an array up to 5 by 5 and write a repeated-addition equation.
Draw shapes with given angles or sides; name common flat shapes and cubes; find faces of solids.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Measure an object's length with a suitable tool.
Compare results of measuring one object with two different units.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, yards, centimeters and meters.
Measure to find how much longer one object is than another.
Solve length problems within 100 by adding or subtracting same-unit lengths.
Use a number line to show whole numbers and to add or subtract within 100.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes with a.m. and p.m.
Read digital time as hours and minutes and match it to the same time on an analog clock.
Find the value of a mix of bills and coins, using dollar and cent signs.
Find different coin combinations that make a given amount.
Make a line plot of number data on a whole-number scale.
Measure lengths to the nearest whole unit and show the data on a line plot.
Draw a picture graph or bar graph for data with up to four categories.
Solve problems using line plots, picture graphs and bar graphs.
Make conclusions from data shown in line plots, pictographs and bar graphs.
Round whole numbers to the closest ten or hundred.
Read and write whole numbers to 100,000 in digits, words and expanded form.
Add and subtract within 1,000 fluently.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 from 10 to 90.
Understand a unit fraction as one of the equal parts of a whole.
Use a fraction for part of an equally split whole; explain numerator and denominator.
Place fractions on a number line, treating 0 to 1 as the whole split into equal parts.
Explain that equivalent fractions name equal amounts or land on one spot on a number line.
Recognize and make equivalent fractions with models and explain why they are equal.
Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator using >, = or <, and justify.
Explain why fractions can only be compared when they refer to the same whole.
Interpret a product as a number of equal groups.
Interpret a quotient as equal sharing or as a number of equal groups.
Describe a story or drawing that shows a multiplication or division situation.
Solve multiplication and division problems within 100.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation with three numbers.
Use properties of operations as strategies for multiplying and dividing.
Multiply and divide within 100 with strategies, and know all one-digit products.
Multiply with products up to 100 fluently.
Write and solve two-step problems with an unknown using any of the four operations.
Check whether answers make sense using mental math, estimation and rounding.
Find patterns in arithmetic and explain them with properties of operations.
Know that shapes in different groups can share features that define a larger group.
Recognize rhombuses and rectangles as quadrilaterals and draw quadrilaterals that are neither.
Split shapes into parts with equal area and name each part as a unit fraction.
Read clocks and write times to the exact minute.
Estimate lengths of time in minutes.
Solve problems that add or subtract minutes.
Measure or estimate the length, liquid volume and weight of objects.
Solve problems with any operation on lengths, liquid volumes or weights in the same units.
Find area by covering a flat shape with unit squares, leaving no gaps or overlaps.
Write area measurements in square units.
Show that tiling a rectangle and multiplying its sides give the same area.
Multiply whole-number side lengths to solve rectangle area problems.
Find the different rectangles that can be made with a given area.
Split a rectangle into smaller rectangles and add their areas to find the whole area.
Solve problems about the perimeter of polygons.
Understand rectangles can share a perimeter but differ in area, or share an area but differ in perimeter.
Make frequency tables and scaled picture and bar graphs for data with several categories.
Solve one- and two-step problems using bar graphs or picture graphs.
Make a line plot to show a set of data.
Answer questions using data shown on a line plot.
Round large whole numbers to whatever place is asked.
Read and write whole numbers to one million in digits, words and expanded form.
Compare two multi-digit numbers with >, = or < and justify.
Know each digit is worth ten times what it would be in the place to its right.
Add and subtract whole numbers fluently.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits, and justify.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders, and justify.
Explain or show with models why two fractions are equivalent.
Recognize and make equivalent fractions.
Compare two fractions with >, = or < and justify.
Understand adding and subtracting fractions as joining and separating parts of the same whole.
Break a fraction into a sum of same-denominator fractions and record it as an equation.
Solve problems that add or subtract same-denominator fractions or mixed numbers.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number by extending what multiplication means.
Solve problems that multiply a fraction by a whole number.
Write fractions with denominators 10 or 100 as decimals.
Understand that a fraction and a decimal can name the same amount.
Read and write decimals to hundredths in words, digits and expanded form.
Compare two decimals to hundredths with >, = or < and justify.
Multiply or divide to solve multiplicative comparison problems.
Solve multi-step whole-number problems with all four operations and unknowns; estimate to check.
Solve division problems with unknowns where the remainder must be interpreted, and justify.
See that a number is a multiple of each factor it has; list a number's multiples.
Tell if a number up to 100 is prime or composite and list all its factor pairs.
Create a number pattern from a stated rule.
State the rule of a given pattern in words or symbols.
Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Classify flat shapes by their sides and angles.
Draw lines of symmetry for flat figures.
Identify angles and estimate their size.
Draw and measure angles in whole degrees with a protractor.
Know the relative sizes of units in one system and convert larger units to smaller.
Solve problems with all four operations about distance, time, liquid volume, weight and money.
Solve rectangle problems with the area and perimeter formulas.
Show measurement data in a frequency table or line plot.
Solve addition and subtraction problems using data from a display.
Analyze data in frequency tables, line plots, bar graphs and picture graphs.
Read and write numbers from billions to thousandths in words, digits and expanded form.
Compare two numbers from billions to thousandths with >, = or < and justify.
Know a digit is worth one tenth of what it would be in the place to its left.
Find values of powers of 10 and connect them to place value.
Round numbers from the billions place to the thousandths place.
Add and subtract large whole numbers and thousandths decimals, and explain the result.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers and decimals to hundredths, and justify.
Divide whole numbers and decimals to hundredths, up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors.
Understand that part of a whole can be written as a fraction or a decimal.
Rewrite a decimal as a fraction and a fraction as a decimal.
Compare and order fractions and decimals to thousandths with >, = or <, and justify.
Estimate sums, differences and products of fractions and decimals to thousandths.
Judge whether a fraction product is reasonable by comparing it to the factors.
Solve and justify problems adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators.
Multiply fractions by fractions or whole numbers, linking fraction products to rectangle areas.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions with models and equations.
Make two number patterns from two rules, graph them as ordered pairs, and relate them.
Write a rule that describes a given number pattern.
Write, evaluate and interpret number expressions using the order of operations.
Turn word descriptions into expressions with numbers and symbols.
Solve and justify multi-step problems with unknowns, whole numbers, fractions and decimals.
Know that features of a shape category belong to all its subcategories.
Classify shapes in a hierarchy based on their properties.
Describe the faces, edges and other features of prisms and pyramids.
Understand volume as measured in unit cubes, and find prism volume by stacking layers.
Use the volume formulas for rectangular prisms with whole-number edges.
Describe the first-quadrant coordinate plane: axes, origin and ordered pairs as distances.
Graph points in the first quadrant and explain what their coordinates mean.
Convert capacity, length and weight units within one measurement system.
Solve multi-step problems that need unit conversions.
Make a line graph for a data set and use it to answer questions.
Make a line plot for a data set, solve problems from it, and find outliers and the median.

state_code: # SOURCES (Missouri Learning Standards: Mathematics Grade-Level Expectations, adopted by the State Board April 2016, in use since 2016-17)
# - K-5 standards PDF (page says to use the Excel file for codes): https://dese.mo.gov/sites/g/files/zuston521/files/media/pdf/2026/04/curr-mls-standards-math-k-5-sboe-2016_AOD.pdf
# - K-12 Excel with full codes (source of the 201 K-5 codes here): https://dese.mo.gov/media/59026/download
# - Official crosswalks, 2016 MLS vs 2010 MLS (= CCSS): https://dese.mo.gov/sites/g/files/zuston521/files/media/pdf/2021/04/cur-mls-crosswalk-ma-gr{k,1,2,3,4,5}.pdf
# - Code format: grade.STRAND.cluster-letter.number (e.g. K.NS.A.1, 4.RA.B.5); expectation numbers run on across clusters within a strand.
#   Some expectations have lettered sub-expectations (a, b, ...) in the Excel; they are folded into their parent row, per the brief.
# - Missouri Student Mathematical Practices are skipped.
# - NS = Number Sense (K-1); NBT = Number Sense and Operations in Base Ten; NF = Number Sense and Operations in Fractions (3-5);
#   RA = Relationships and Algebraic Thinking; GM = Geometry and Measurement; DS = Data and Statistics
# - DESE lists as having no counterpart: 4.NF.C.5 (tenths to hundredths, adding them), 4.MD.C.7 (angle measure is additive), 5.NF.B.3 (fraction as division).
#   Note: the same crosswalk lines up MO 5.NF.A.2 (convert decimals/fractions) with 5.NF.B.3, so that link is kept here as "edited".
# - Not in any row here: 4.MD.C.7 and 4.NF.C.5 (as DESE says). Partly dropped: 3.NF.A.3c (whole numbers as fractions), 5.NF.B.7c word problems,
#   2.NBT.A.2 skip-count by 5s is in MO grade 1 (1.NS.A.4).
# - Counting backward (K.NS.A.3, 1.NS.A.3), subitizing to 5 (K.NS.B.8), counting by 10s from any number (1.NBT.A.4).
# - Time and calendar in K (K.GM.B.3, K.GM.B.4); coins in K and 1 (K.GM.B.5, 1.GM.C.9, marked moved from 2.MD.C.8); coin combinations (2.GM.D.13).
# - Seeing shapes from different views (1.GM.A.3); prisms and pyramids (5.GM.A.3); line graphs (5.DS.A.1); outliers and median (5.DS.A.2, ~6.SP).
# - Place value: to 100,000 in grade 3 (3.NBT.A.2, moved from 4.NBT.A.2) and billions in grade 5 (5.NBT.A.1, 5.NBT.A.2, 5.NBT.A.5).
# - Prime/composite kept in grade 4 (4.RA.B.5); order of operations named in 5.RA.B.3; frequency tables in grades 3-4.
# - The DESE crosswalk is a two-column table where one CCSS cell often spans several MO rows. Rows with no CCSS beside them were matched to the
#   CCSS standard of that span by reading content (e.g. K.NS.B.6-7 -> K.CC.B.4, 1.GM.B.6 -> 1.MD.A.1, 3.GM.C.12-14 -> 3.MD.C.7, 4.NF.B.5-6 -> 4.NF.B.3).
# - DESE oddities kept: 1.RA.B.5 also lists 1.OA.C.5; 2.NBT.B.6 also lists 2.NBT.B.9; 3.RA.B.6 also lists 3.OA.B.6. DESE typos fixed: K.G.B.3 -> K.G.A.3, K.G.A.4 -> K.G.B.4, K.0A -> K.OA.
# - Changed from DESE: DESE puts CCSS 5.NF.B.6 (multiply fractions, word problems) beside MO 5.NF.B.6 (add/subtract); here it sits with 5.NF.B.7 (multiply).
#   5.RA.C.5 (DESE: 5.NBT.B.7 only) also gets 5.NF.A.2, 5.NF.B.6, 5.NF.B.7 because it covers fraction problems too.
# - "same" vs "edited": a MO expectation that restates one CCSS sub-part (a/b/c) is "same"; one that splits a CCSS sentence or changes scope is "edited".
# - DESE posted a re-tagged K-5 PDF in April 2026 (file name ends _AOD); its content still says Spring 2016. No newer MO math standards were found.
